case_number: C.A. No. 786 of 2022 and C.A. No. 787 of 2022 (Arising out of SLP(C) No. 16671 of 2021 and SLP(C) No. 16672 of 2021)
summary: Dispute over technical disqualification of respondent's bid in a tender for supply of tablets; issue centered on interpretation of 'same or similar Category Products' under 'Past Performance' criterion—whether supply of smartphones qualifies as similar to tablets; High Court intervened, setting aside technical rejection; appellant challenged justification for judicial interference in tender evaluation. Court examined tender conditions, scope of judicial review in procurement, and reasonableness of classification. Held that while tendering authorities have domain expertise, arbitrary or irrational exclusions attract judicial scrutiny.
legal_provisions_cited: Principles of judicial review in administrative action
Contract law principles in public procurement
final_judgment: Appeals allowed in part; impugned order of High Court set aside; restoration of status quo ante; matter remanded to tender authority for fresh evaluation consistent with reasoned application of tender criteria and principles of fairness.
